name: San Marino
summary_text: San Marino is workable for trans visitors — safe in practice, thin in law. ILGA-Europe lists San Marino among states with no functioning legal gender recognition process (resident-facing gap only). There is no criminalisation, no bathroom law, no border friction (open border with Italy), and no documented pattern of anti-trans violence in this tiny, tourism-dependent republic surrounded by Italy. The score reflects very high de facto safety combined with minimal explicit legal infrastructure for trans people. Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.title: Legal gender recognition - Rainbow Map
sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Rainbow Map legal gender recognition category page (2026): San Marino is listed among countries with no functioning legal or administrative process for legal gender recognition; self-determination-based recognition exists in 12 countries (Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Luxembourg, Malta, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Switzerland).

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 - Legal Gender Recognition chapter: country-by-country findings for 2025, including Albania's rejection of a self-ID recommendation at UPR, trans activist Luana Myrto's legal action in Albania, Andorra's delayed hormone-treatment decree, and other European developments.

ILGA compilation of SOGIESC recommendations from the 34th UPR Working Group session (Nov 2019) - includes San Marino's review among 12 countries examined; documents the SOGIESC recommendations each state received and accepted.

sources.title: San Marino bans discrimination based on sexual orientation | Euronews
sources.claim_summary: Euronews (June 2019): San Marino banned discrimination based on sexual orientation (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

sources.title: San Marino appoints world’s first openly gay head of state | San Marino | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (April 2022): San Marino appointed the world's first openly gay head of state - Paolo Rondelli named one of two captains regent in 'a country making strides on gay rights'.

sources.title: San Marino approva legge sulle unioni civili: "Più snella rispetto alla Cirinnà" | Euronews
sources.claim_summary: Euronews Italian (Nov 2018, in Italian): San Marino approved a civil-unions law, leaner than Italy's Cirinnà law - the legislative milestone for relationship recognition.
